title: pkcs1: rename to pkixalgs
description:
PKCS \#1 is the standard that defines RSA, but this dissector hasn't been limited
to RSA since commit 9e4afbfd49. Now it covers all asymmetric key algorithms
defined by RFC 3279 and its updates.

Given the expanded scope of this dissector, it seems prudent to rename it.

notes.body: I do not have an opinion on this change, but you should at a minimum use proto_register_alias() to ensure backward compatibility as here you are breaking all existing filters.

@pquantin it is good for you now ?
I still have no opinion on whether we should rename it or not, by having the alias now is the right thing to do.

I'm a little confused because while I think the proto_register_alias() call is necessary, what is it supposed to affect?  My confusion comes from the PFNAME name originally being "pkcs-1", which doesn't match any of the field filters (that were all prefixed with "pkcs1"), and that seems like a bug 20 years in the making (based on original copyright of 2004).
So I think the current proto_register_alias() call will work for the individual fields, but not if a user just wants "all packets of the protocol" and types in "pkcs-1" because that's what the "protocol ID name" used to be?
There isn't such a thing as a "PKCS#1 packet", since this dissector just provides data structures for other dissectors to use. So typing in just `pkcs-1` wouldn't have done anything useful anyway.
I see that now.  The generated ASN.1 dissectors can throw me for a loop from time to time with how their dissection works.
